key_insight: The paper replaces prescribed turbulence covariance with a solved displacement-volatility field that is coupled directly to resolved velocity through Itô–Hencky kinematics and a source-consistent stochastic momentum balance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a theoretically grounded closure architecture for stochastic CFD, with potential for better handling of wall constraints, energy transfer, and finite-correlation turbulence effects.
method: Uses a one-channel Itô configuration map with matrix-logarithm Hencky increments and exact volume-preserving constraints.
Derives a source-consistent pull-back momentum equation retaining momentum-source covariation and yielding an index-one DAE system.
Constructs a finite-correlation Green–Kubo precursor and accounts for state-dependent Lyapunov drift plus boundary reaction work.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivations and limiting-case consistency checks, but no numerical turbulence data or CFD validation yet.
watch_item: The framework is theory-complete but still unvalidated in developed turbulent statistics and CFD benchmarks, so practical robustness remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Foundations of a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure: Itô--Hencky kinematics, source-consistent momentum and finite-correlation realisation
